identification: Ten hand-made studio pottery 'Widecombe Fair' (Widdicombe Fair) novelty figures by Will Young of Widecombe-in-the-Moor, Devon (Runnaford Pottery / 'Pickwick' pottery), each signed 'Will Young / Widecombe' on the base and named on the base: Old Grey Mare, 'Arry Awke, Dan'l Whiddon, Jan Stewer, Old Uncle Tom Cobley in his chair (back inscribed 'Old Uncle Tom Cobley in his famous chair at Widecombe in the Moor'), Tom Pearse, Peter Gurney, Peter Davy, Bill Brewer, plus a standing Uncle Tom Cobley with both arms and a pipe snapped off (loose pieces shown). Together with a framed vintage colour comic-strip print 'Widdicombe Fair' (chorus 'With Bill Brewer, Jan Stewer, Peter Gurney, Peter Davy, Dan'l Widden, 'Arry 'Awke an' auld Uncle Tom Cobleigh an' all', 'Copyright Registered' line too small to read), in a dark timber frame, stuck down and with mount toning. Catalogue says some damage; the standing Cobley is clearly broken.

viewing_check: Estimate $60-90, no bids yet (opening $20). Ten figures sold as a lot for GBP130 (about A$260) in Dec 2025 and singles sell about A$25-40 each on eBay UK, so ten could be worth A$250-350 if sold singly, but one standing Uncle Tom Cobley is broken (arms off) and others may be chipped: check every figure for chips/cracks, and that the signature is on each base (unsigned ones are worth less). The print is only of modest value (dealer asks GBP125 for a framed one; unclear if same edition). Prices are 1-2 years old, stable. UK sold prices include UK postage buyers pay; Australian resale is thin (no AU eBay sales found in 3 years).
